source.name: sp_BuildMonthlyReport

result.generatedDdl:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION dbo.sp_BuildMonthlyReport(
    p_year INT,
    p_month INT
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    customername TEXT,
    ordercount BIGINT,
    totalrevenue NUMERIC(12,2)
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    -- Temp table usage
    CREATE TEMP TABLE IF NOT EXISTS temp_monthlystats (
        customerid INT,
        ordercount INT,
        totalrevenue NUMERIC(12,2)
    ) ON COMMIT DROP;

    INSERT INTO temp_monthlystats
    SELECT
        o.customerid,
        COUNT(*)::INT,
        SUM(o.totalamount)
    FROM dbo.orders o
    WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.orderdate) = p_year 
      AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.orderdate) = p_month
    GROUP BY o.customerid;

    -- Return results joined with customer info
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT
        c.firstname || ' ' || c.lastname AS customername,
        ms.ordercount::BIGINT,
        ms.totalrevenue
    FROM temp_monthlystats ms
    INNER JOIN dbo.customers c ON ms.customerid = c.customerid
    ORDER BY ms.totalrevenue DESC;

    -- Temp table automatically dropped on commit
END;
$$;
assumptions: The procedure returns a result set, so it is converted to a FUNCTION returning TABLE
Parameter names prefixed with 'p_' to follow PostgreSQL conventions and avoid conflicts
DECIMAL(12,2) mapped to NUMERIC(12,2) in PostgreSQL
COUNT(*) returns BIGINT in PostgreSQL, explicitly cast to INT for temp table compatibility
String concatenation using '+' converted to '||' operator
YEAR() and MONTH() functions converted to EXTRACT(YEAR/MONTH FROM ...)
Temporary table created with ON COMMIT DROP to auto-cleanup after function execution
SET NOCOUNT ON has no direct equivalent in PostgreSQL and is omitted (PostgreSQL functions don't return row counts by default)
Schema 'dbo' is preserved assuming it exists in PostgreSQL database
Customers table has firstname and lastname columns (case-sensitive names converted to lowercase per PostgreSQL default)

compatibilityNotes.description: SQL Server: EXEC dbo.sp_BuildMonthlyReport @Year=2024, @Month=1; PostgreSQL: SELECT * FROM dbo.sp_BuildMonthlyReport(2024, 1);
Converted from PROCEDURE to FUNCTION returning TABLE. This changes how the object is invoked and how results are consumed.
PostgreSQL temporary tables are session-scoped by default. Using ON COMMIT DROP ensures cleanup after function execution, but behavior may differ in complex transaction scenarios.
COUNT(*) returns BIGINT in PostgreSQL vs INT in SQL Server. Explicit casting applied where needed for consistency.
PostgreSQL uses || for concatenation. NULL values in concatenation may behave differently; consider using CONCAT() function if NULL handling is critical.
YEAR()/MONTH() converted to EXTRACT(). Performance characteristics may differ; consider adding functional indexes if this query is performance-critical.
